findings.issue_text: [BUG] The webauthn-absence assertions in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey are swallowed no-ops because catch(Exception) also catches the AssertionError raised by fail(). In both blocks the test does assertThat(driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']"), nullValue()) inside a try and then fail(). If the webauthn form IS present, findElement succeeds, assertThat(...) throws AssertionError, which is caught by catch (Exception nsee) and silently discarded; if absent, fail() throws AssertionError which is likewise caught. Either way the test proceeds past the check, so the regression it claims to guard (passkeys UI leaking into re-auth for a user without passkeys) would pass CI without failing — the reviewer and future maintainers get false confidence that this behavior is covered.

[ADVISORY] The new protected isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) in UsernamePasswordForm shares its name but not its semantics with the no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() that UsernameForm.authenticate calls at line 47 of UsernameForm.java. Two sibling classes extending AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator now expose identically-named methods with different signatures and different truth conditions (one apparently flow/feature-based, the other user-null-based), so a future maintainer refactoring 'conditional passkeys' checks will conflate them and change one site's behavior while believing both are the same predicate; the next change to passkey gating gets riskier because the diff introduces the collision.

[BUG] UsernameForm.authenticate() calls a no-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() that is defined nowhere in the diff or in the class's shown hierarchy (the only definition added is UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel), and UsernameForm extends AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, not UsernamePasswordForm), and even if such a helper exists it is invoked with no access to the user/realm in scope of the shown code, so the gate cannot consult the session context the sibling UsernamePasswordForm version uses. Either the module fails to compile, or UsernameForm silently runs a different (context-free) passkeys check than UsernamePasswordForm, so the username form skip/force decision diverges between the two entry points and one of them re-authenticates the wrong way.

[ADVISORY] reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey is named for 'user without passkey' but actually sets setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE), so it only verifies the realm-passkeys-disabled path; the real edge case it claims to cover — a user with no WebAuthn credential while the realm passkeys policy is ENABLED and conditional UI is active during re-auth — is never exercised, even though WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm now unconditionally enters the user-identified branch when user != null (WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:101-103) and the empty-authenticators path (authenticators.isEmpty()) there has no test asserting what the form renders. A user with password-only credentials in a passkeys-enabled realm hitting re-auth gets an unverified form state (empty authenticator list, isUserIdentified false, fallthrough to passwordless bean) — a regression there ships untested.

[ADVISORY] The new setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError (USERNAME_HIDDEN / REGISTRATION_DISABLED attributes set after failed password during re-auth) has no test in the diff asserting either attribute: the added re-auth tests assert only the webauth form presence and error text, and never assert the username field is hidden or registration link suppressed after the failed-password challenge. A regression that leaks the username input or the registration link onto the re-auth error page (the exact bug the extracted helper exists to prevent) would pass the entire new test suite unchanged.

[ADVISORY] shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() hard-returns false unconditionally, removing the user-identified rendering branch for every use of this authenticator, including configurations where WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator is placed as a second-factor execution after the user is identified — the two-factor page for this authenticator now never lists the user's authenticators and the isUserIdentified=true form attributes from that branch (WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:101-119) are unreachable for this subclass, with no test covering a conditional-UI authenticator used in an identified-user/2FA flow. Admins who had the conditional UI authenticator in a 2FA position (or step-up flows where user is set by a prior execution) get a silent behavior change: authenticator selection UI disappears and the form falls into the passwordless/discoverable rendering regardless of flow position.

[ADVISORY] The UsernameForm change skips the previous auto-success for an already-set user whenever passkeys are enabled, but the only tests added exercise UsernamePasswordForm-based flows; there is no test for a UsernameForm flow where context.getUser() != null with passkeys enabled, so the newly reachable path (username form shown during re-auth instead of auto-advancing, including the interaction with hasLinkedBrokers) is entirely unverified. Realms using the standalone Username Form execution (username + password as separate executions) get a changed re-auth behavior — user is shown a username form during re-auth — with no assertion anywhere in the diff that the page renders, the user is preserved, and linked-broker users still skip correctly; a regression in this branch ships silently.

[ADVISORY] The new `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` guard on the re-auth skip path is keyed on realm-wide passkeys enablement, not on whether this user can actually use a passkey. A user whose only re-authentication path is a linked broker (no password, no webauthn credential) in a realm where passkeys are enabled now gets the username form instead of being routed straight to their broker — the re-auth flow dead-ends in a form they cannot complete; this behavior change is not traceable to the 'fix re-authentication with passkeys' intent and no test covers the broker+passkeys-enabled combination.

[ADVISORY] fillContextForm now runs during re-authentication whenever the user is set (via UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled), and the base shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators only checks user != null — not whether the user has any webauthn credential — so the authenticators.isEmpty() branch is reachable for password-only users in passkeys-enabled realms. A user with no webauthn credential re-authenticating in a realm with passkeys enabled hits the empty-authenticators error path and can get a spurious 'webauthn-authenticator-support'-style error message rendered on the username/password re-auth page; the added test reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey only covers the passkeys-disabled realm, so this user class is untested.

[ADVISORY] The util package now statically imports a constant from the browser package, and AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator's constant was widened to public solely to support it, creating a browser ↔ util package cycle and a leaked internal protocol flag. The next refactor of the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth-note key must now touch two packages in lockstep, and the marker that previously scoped the re-auth handshake inside the browser authenticators is now consumable by any util caller with no contract documented.

[ADVISORY] The referenced method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() (no-arg) is not defined anywhere in this diff for UsernameForm, so the diff relies on a helper whose provenance and semantics (realm check only, ignoring the current user) cannot be traced to any stated requirement here. If the helper is missing or resolves passkeys state differently than UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) (which takes a user and combines three conditions), the two authenticators diverge on the same decision and the re-auth flow renders inconsistent pages; reviewers and future maintainers cannot verify the invariant from this change alone.

[ADVISORY] Calling AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError inside createErrorResponse applies username-hiding/registration-disabling to the conditional-UI passkey error page, which is a distinct error surface (a webauthn form, not a username/password form) from the util method's documented purpose. During re-auth, a failed conditional-UI passkey attempt now silently sets USERNAME_HIDDEN and REGISTRATION_DISABLED attributes on a page that does not render a username field, so the call is either inert (dead coupling) or alters a theme that does honor those attributes in unexpected ways; the method's name and comment claim a username/password form context that this call site does not provide.

[BUG] The challenge(error) overload inverts the original user-identity gate: it previously called webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) only when context.getUser() == null (i.e. during initial login, exactly the case WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator exists for), and the new code calls it only when the user IS set. A user who fails their first password attempt (context.getUser() still null in the combined username/password form) gets an error page with no conditional-UI passkey data — the passkey autofill option that the original code deliberately rendered on the unidentified-user error page disappears, so a passkey-only user who mistypes a password can no longer switch to passkey from that error page.

[BUG] The authenticate() path now gates fillContextForm on isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which returns false when the user is null, while the pre-change comment and challenge() condition show this setup was intended for the not-yet-identified user (conditional passkey autofill on the initial username/password page). On a fresh first-time login (context.getUser() == null) with passkeys enabled in the realm, fillContextForm is never invoked, so the ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI flag and username-autocomplete ('username webauthn') never get set on the initial login page — the primary conditional-UI passkey entry point for unidentified users is silently dropped from this form.

[ADVISORY] UsernameForm calls a no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() while UsernamePasswordForm (a sibling subclass of AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator) defines a one-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) whose semantics additionally require user != null — two confusable same-stem identifiers with different semantics in adjacent classes of the same hierarchy. The next maintainer editing re-auth/passkey gating will reasonably assume the two methods are the same predicate and change one expecting the other to follow; because the one-arg variant smuggles a 'user is identified' requirement into a method whose name only promises 'passkeys enabled', a call site that means only the feature check will silently skip conditional UI when the user is null — the exact class of bug this diff itself was fixing.

[ADVISORY] shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators is a protected hook on WebAuthnAuthenticator that only WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator overrides to return false, producing a base-vs-subclass contradiction: the base class's fillContextForm doc/behavior says 'show authenticators when user identified', while the conditional-UI subclass must never show them — the dispatch decision 'conditional UI never lists authenticators' is encoded as an inverted override rather than as data on the shared helper. Any future subclass of WebAuthnAuthenticator (or new call site of fillContextForm) inherits the 'list authenticators when user != null' behavior and will render the authenticator list during conditional-UI re-auth unless it remembers to duplicate this override; the invariant lives in one subclass instead of in the shared code path, so the next authenticator variant gets it wrong.

[BUG] The diff silently inverts a previously human-accepted behavior contract by rewriting assertions that passkeys were disabled after username selection into assertions that passkeys remain enabled. The prior test encoded an accepted product decision: after a user is identified in a conditional-passkeys realm, the webauthn form was removed ('passkeys username password page should be presented with username selected and passkeys disabled'). This diff flips both the comment and the assertion (NoSuchElementException → NotNull) with no product-level rationale in the PR title or description, so realms that rely on the old behavior (no passkey prompt once user is identified) get a behavior change shipped inside a bugfix PR. Whoever accepted the original assertion never accepted its reversal.

[ADVISORY] The new gate `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` changes re-authentication behavior for every passkeys-enabled realm, including users who hold no passkey credential at all, which is broader than the stated intent of 'fixing re-authentication with passkeys'. A user with only a password in a passkeys-enabled realm who previously sailed through UsernameForm during re-auth now gets a username/password challenge every time; the new test reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey bakes in this broadened behavior, converting a side effect of the fix into the accepted spec without an explicit decision that password-only users should lose the re-auth fast path in passkeys realms.

[ADVISORY] Replacing the direct `user != null` check with the overridable shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context) hook, which the conditional-UI subclass hard-codes to false, silently disables the existing two-factor WebAuthn page's authenticator list in the conditional flow without that being part of the stated fix. The WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator subclass (WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:63-65) returns false unconditionally, so any deployment where the conditional-UI authenticator was rendering the authenticator picker in a 2FA step now gets the generic non-identified form instead; this is an objective change to the 2FA render path shipped under a re-auth bugfix title, and out-of-tree subclasses of WebAuthnAuthenticator that did not anticipate the new hook inherit the old behavior while conditional-UI users silently lose theirs.

[ADVISORY] shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() is hard-overridden to false, so WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm never populates the user's authenticator list on any conditional-UI page, including the error path createErrorResponse which still calls fillContextForm. A user whose webauthn authenticator is used with an identified user (2-factor or error re-challenge) gets a webauthn form with no authenticators rendered; after a failed passkey attempt the error page offers no list/button to retry with a specific credential, leaving the re-authentication flow stuck and pushing users to password fallback even when a passkey is their only usable credential.

[ADVISORY] The webauthn form setup was moved out of the user==null branch but is now gated on isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) which requires user != null, so on a fresh (non-reauth) login where no user is preset, fillContextForm is never invoked and the conditional-UI/discoverable-passkey data (previously set up for the anonymous username/password page) is no longer populated. Realms using the combined UsernamePasswordForm with passkeys enabled lose discoverable-passkey autofill on the initial login page; first-time logins must fall back to password, which both degrades the phishing-resistant path and contradicts the test expectation that the //form[@id='webauth'] element be present for anonymous users (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithExternalKey).

[ADVISORY] When context.getUser() is already set during re-authentication and conditional passkeys are enabled, the skip-to-success shortcut is disabled and the plain username form is rendered, but the form still allows submitting a different username on a re-authentication session whose target user is fixed. During prompt=login re-authentication the user is presented an editable username field on a session already bound to a user; if the downstream validation of the re-auth flow does not enforce that the presented credential belongs to the original user, an attacker with an active session could pivot the re-auth toward a different account identity — the flow should be audited to confirm the error path (badPasswordHandler) and webauthn assertion both re-bind to the original user only.

[BUG] The first 'webauthn button absent' check in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey asserts nothing because the catch(Exception) swallows the AssertionError from assertThat(..., nullValue()). If the webauthn form is wrongly rendered on the initial login page (the exact regression the test exists to catch), assertThat throws AssertionError, which is caught by catch(Exception nsee), the fail() line is never reached, and the test still passes green — the assertion provides zero verification of 'passkeys should not be shown'.

[BUG] The second 'webauthn button absent' check in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey has the same try/catch swallowing the AssertionError, and additionally the enclosing catch makes the fail() call unreachable whenever findElement succeeds. The re-authentication page assertion 'passkeys login should not be available as this user does not have a passkey' is unconditionally satisfied: both outcomes (element absent -> NoSuchElementException caught; element present -> AssertionError caught) lead to a passing test, so the core claim of this new test is never actually verified.

[ADVISORY] No test in the diff asserts the actual effect of setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError — that USERNAME_HIDDEN and REGISTRATION_DISABLED are set on the form when re-authentication fails. The re-authentication tests (webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey) assert the error message and the presence of the webauthn form after a bad password, but never assert that the username input is hidden or registration is disabled; a regression that re-displays the username field on the re-auth error page (the original bug this refactor re-implements) would pass all new tests. Checked: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java, PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java, PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.java contain no assertion of a hidden username field or registration-disabled state.

[ADVISORY] webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication (and its copy in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest) never verifies the login form was actually shown before the re-auth login — the test opens prompt=login and immediately asserts appPage.assertCurrent(), so it cannot distinguish conditional-UI auto-login from the browser reusing the existing SSO session. If the prompt=login re-auth request were silently satisfied by the existing session without any passkey ceremony (defeating the point of re-authentication), the appPage.assertCurrent() and the LOGIN event assertion would still pass because the event details match the earlier auto-login pattern; a regression where UsernameForm skips and SSO short-circuits re-auth would go undetected. The author's counter-argument is that events.expectLogin().assertEvent() would fail if no new LOGIN event is produced — but a reuse of the prior session can still emit a LOGIN event with the same details, so the finding survives.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The webauthn-absence assertions in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey are swallowed no-ops because catch(Exception) also catches the AssertionError raised by fail(). In both blocks the test does assertThat(driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']"), nullValue()) inside a try and then fail(). If the webauthn form IS present, findElement succeeds, assertThat(...) throws AssertionError, which is caught by catch (Exception nsee) and silently discarded; if absent, fail() throws AssertionError which is likewise caught. Either way the test proceeds past the check, so the regression it claims to guard (passkeys UI leaking into re-auth for a user without passkeys) would pass CI without failing — the reviewer and future maintainers get false confidence that this behavior is covered.

adjudication.rationale: In `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, both checks use `try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception ...) {}`. The finding claims the `catch(Exception)` swallows the `AssertionError` from `fail()` / `assertThat`, making the assertion a no-op. But `AssertionError` is an `Error`, not an `Exception`, so it is not caught by `catch (Exception nsee)`. If the element is present, `assertThat(element, nullValue())` throws `AssertionError` and the test fails. If the element is absent, `findElement` throws (typically `NoSuchElementException`, an `Exception`) and the catch executes as intended. So the described swallowing behavior is not supported by the diff.

This helper is now invoked on password failure (`AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler`) and conditional-passkey error (`WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse`). The newly added/modified tests in the diff assert WebAuthn form presence and error/info messages, but do not assert that the username field is hidden or registration is disabled on the re-authentication error page, so a regression in these attributes could go undetected by the tests shown.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes the finding’s core claim verifiable: `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` now gates the “user already identified / list authenticators” branch on `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` (was effectively `user != null`), and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` overrides `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators()` to unconditionally return `false`. That means for this subclass the identified-user branch (and associated `isUserIdentified`/authenticator-list attributes) is unreachable regardless of flow position. However, from the diff alone it’s not provably a defect because the override is explicitly documented as intentional (“Do not show authenticators during login with conditional passkeys”), but it does represent a potentially significant behavior change for configurations that previously relied on the identified-user listing, and the diff does not add a test covering conditional-UI authenticator in an identified-user/2FA placement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The UsernameForm change skips the previous auto-success for an already-set user whenever passkeys are enabled, but the only tests added exercise UsernamePasswordForm-based flows; there is no test for a UsernameForm flow where context.getUser() != null with passkeys enabled, so the newly reachable path (username form shown during re-auth instead of auto-advancing, including the interaction with hasLinkedBrokers) is entirely unverified. adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `UsernameForm.authenticate` to *not* auto-`success()` when `context.getUser() != null` if passkeys are enabled (`if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`), which makes a previously skipped path reachable during re-authentication flows using the standalone Username Form execution. The newly reachable behavior (showing/processing the username form during re-auth, and the existing `hasLinkedBrokers(context)` exception logic) is not directly asserted anywhere in the added/modified tests; the added re-authentication tests mainly assert eventual success/events and WebAuthn presence, not that the UsernameForm page renders correctly in this specific scenario nor that linked-broker behavior remains correct. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap rather than a provable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` guard on the re-auth skip path is keyed on realm-wide passkeys enablement, not on whether this user can actually use a passkey. A user whose only re-authentication path is a linked broker (no password, no webauthn credential) in a realm where passkeys are enabled now gets the username form instead of being routed straight to their broker — the re-auth flow dead-ends in a form they cannot complete; this behavior change is not traceable to the 'fix re-authentication with passkeys' intent and no test covers the broker+passkeys-enabled combination.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `UsernameForm.authenticate()` now skips the re-auth username form only when `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (previously it skipped whenever `context.getUser() != null`, subject to `hasLinkedBrokers`). This ties the skip behavior to passkeys/conditional-UI enablement rather than to whether the current user can actually authenticate with a passkey. That is a concrete, diff-grounded behavior change that could add an extra username step for re-auth in passkeys-enabled realms even for users without passkeys. However, the finding’s specific “broker-only user dead-ends / routed straight to their broker” claim is not verifiable from this diff: users with linked brokers already did not take the skip path (the code still checks `hasLinkedBrokers(context)`), and nothing in the shown changes demonstrates a dead-end or broker routing logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] fillContextForm now runs during re-authentication whenever the user is set (via UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled), and the base shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators only checks user != null — not whether the user has any webauthn credential — so the authenticators.isEmpty() branch is reachable for password-only users in passkeys-enabled realms. A user with no webauthn credential re-authenticating in a realm with passkeys enabled hits the empty-authenticators error path and can get a spurious 'webauthn-authenticator-support'-style error message rendered on the username/password re-auth page; the added test reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey only covers the passkeys-disabled realm, so this user class is untested.

adjudication.rationale: The finding assumes UsernamePasswordForm’s new `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` will invoke `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` in a way that reaches the `authenticators.isEmpty()` error path for “password-only users”. However, the diff explicitly adds `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(AuthenticationFlowContext)` returning `false`, and `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` now gates the “load authenticators / if empty setError(webauthn-authenticator-support)” logic behind `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)`. Therefore, for conditional passkeys (the scenario `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` is about), the empty-authenticators error branch is not reachable per this diff. The rest of the claim (spurious error on username/password re-auth page; missing test for passkeys-enabled realm with no webauthn credential) is speculative and not verifiable from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The util package now statically imports a constant from the browser package, and AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator's constant was widened to public solely to support it, creating a browser ↔ util package cycle and a leaked internal protocol flag. The next refactor of the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth-note key must now touch two packages in lockstep, and the marker that previously scoped the re-auth handshake inside the browser authenticators is now consumable by any util caller with no contract documented.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` widened from `protected` to `public` (browser package) specifically so `AuthenticatorUtils` (util package) can `import static ...AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH`. At the same time, browser code now calls `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` (e.g., in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler` and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator`). This creates a concrete cross-package mutual dependency (browser -> util via method call, util -> browser via constant reference) and exposes an auth-note key as a public API surface without any documented contract in the diff. This is an architectural/API-surface concern rather than a directly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The referenced method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() (no-arg) is not defined anywhere in this diff for UsernameForm, so the diff relies on a helper whose provenance and semantics (realm check only, ignoring the current user) cannot be traced to any stated requirement here. If the helper is missing or resolves passkeys state differently than UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) (which takes a user and combines three conditions), the two authenticators diverge on the same decision and the re-auth flow renders inconsistent pages; reviewers and future maintainers cannot verify the invariant from this change alone.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `UsernameForm.authenticate()` now calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (no-arg), but this diff does not show whether that method already exists in `UsernameForm`’s superclass hierarchy or elsewhere in the codebase. Therefore, the finding’s implication that the helper is “not defined anywhere”/potentially missing (or that its semantics necessarily diverge from `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)`) cannot be verified from the diff alone; it’s speculative rather than a diff-provable defect or concrete review issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Calling AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError inside createErrorResponse applies username-hiding/registration-disabling to the conditional-UI passkey error page, which is a distinct error surface (a webauthn form, not a username/password form) from the util method's documented purpose. During re-auth, a failed conditional-UI passkey attempt now silently sets USERNAME_HIDDEN and REGISTRATION_DISABLED attributes on a page that does not render a username field, so the call is either inert (dead coupling) or alters a theme that does honor those attributes in unexpected ways; the method's name and comment claim a username/password form context that this call site does not provide.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse() now calls AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context), which conditionally sets LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN and REGISTRATION_DISABLED on context.form() based on USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH. That utility method is documented/named as targeting “UsernamePassword” form errors, yet it is invoked in a conditional-passkeys WebAuthn error flow (createErrorResponse) before fillContextForm(context). This is a real, diff-grounded coupling/semantic mismatch that could be inert or have unintended theme effects, but the diff alone doesn’t prove it breaks behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The challenge(error) overload inverts the original user-identity gate: it previously called webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) only when context.getUser() == null (i.e. during initial login, exactly the case WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator exists for), and the new code calls it only when the user IS set. A user who fails their first password attempt (context.getUser() still null in the combined username/password form) gets an error page with no conditional-UI passkey data — the passkey autofill option that the original code deliberately rendered on the unidentified-user error page disappears, so a passkey-only user who mistypes a password can no longer switch to passkey from that error page.

[BUG] The authenticate() path now gates fillContextForm on isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which returns false when the user is null, while the pre-change comment and challenge() condition show this setup was intended for the not-yet-identified user (conditional passkey autofill on the initial username/password page). On a fresh first-time login (context.getUser() == null) with passkeys enabled in the realm, fillContextForm is never invoked, so the ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI flag and username-autocomplete ('username webauthn') never get set on the initial login page — the primary conditional-UI passkey entry point for unidentified users is silently dropped from this form.
matched_golden_ids: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same bug: authenticate() now conditions webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which fails when context.getUser() is null on the initial login page. As a result, conditional passkey/ID-less UI setup (flags/autocomplete) is not applied for first-time/unknown-user passkey login.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] UsernameForm calls a no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() while UsernamePasswordForm (a sibling subclass of AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator) defines a one-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) whose semantics additionally require user != null — two confusable same-stem identifiers with different semantics in adjacent classes of the same hierarchy. The next maintainer editing re-auth/passkey gating will reasonably assume the two methods are the same predicate and change one expecting the other to follow; because the one-arg variant smuggles a 'user is identified' requirement into a method whose name only promises 'passkeys enabled', a call site that means only the feature check will silently skip conditional UI when the user is null — the exact class of bug this diff itself was fixing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `UsernameForm.authenticate()` now gating on a no-arg `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (`if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`), while `UsernamePasswordForm` introduces a new overload `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` that additionally requires `user != null` (`return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null;`). These same-stem predicates with different semantics in adjacent authenticators are plausibly confusing/fragile for maintainers (a naming/API clarity issue), even though the current behavior appears intentional (tests added for re-auth with passkeys).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators is a protected hook on WebAuthnAuthenticator that only WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator overrides to return false, producing a base-vs-subclass contradiction: the base class's fillContextForm doc/behavior says 'show authenticators when user identified', while the conditional-UI subclass must never show them — the dispatch decision 'conditional UI never lists authenticators' is encoded as an inverted override rather than as data on the shared helper. Any future subclass of WebAuthnAuthenticator (or new call site of fillContextForm) inherits the 'list authenticators when user != null' behavior and will render the authenticator list during conditional-UI re-auth unless it remembers to duplicate this override; the invariant lives in one subclass instead of in the shared code path, so the next authenticator variant gets it wrong.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new protected hook `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(AuthenticationFlowContext)` in `WebAuthnAuthenticator`, with a default implementation `return context.getUser() != null;`, and changes `fillContextForm` to gate listing authenticators on that hook. `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` then overrides this hook to always return `false` ("Do not show authenticators during login with conditional passkeys"). This works for the current subclass, but it does encode the “conditional UI must never list authenticators” invariant only in that subclass override; any future subclass or new `fillContextForm` usage that doesn’t remember to override will inherit the default “show when user != null” behavior. That’s an architectural/maintainability concern created by this change, not a directly verifiable functional bug in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The diff silently inverts a previously human-accepted behavior contract by rewriting assertions that passkeys were disabled after username selection into assertions that passkeys remain enabled. The prior test encoded an accepted product decision: after a user is identified in a conditional-passkeys realm, the webauthn form was removed ('passkeys username password page should be presented with username selected and passkeys disabled'). This diff flips both the comment and the assertion (NoSuchElementException → NotNull) with no product-level rationale in the PR title or description, so realms that rely on the old behavior (no passkey prompt once user is identified) get a behavior change shipped inside a bugfix PR. Whoever accepted the original assertion never accepted its reversal.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the previously asserted behavior: in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey the comment and assertion are flipped from expecting the WebAuthn form to be absent after username selection (NoSuchElementException) to expecting it to still be present (notNullValue). Corresponding production changes also make passkeys UI setup happen when a user is already identified (e.g., UsernamePasswordForm now calls webauthnAuth.fillContextForm when isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) and isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null). However, from the diff alone this is not verifiably a defect—it appears to be an intentional behavior change (also backed by new re-authentication tests). Claims about lack of product-level rationale in PR title/description are not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new gate `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` changes re-authentication behavior for every passkeys-enabled realm, including users who hold no passkey credential at all, which is broader than the stated intent of 'fixing re-authentication with passkeys'. A user with only a password in a passkeys-enabled realm who previously sailed through UsernameForm during re-auth now gets a username/password challenge every time; the new test reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey bakes in this broadened behavior, converting a side effect of the fix into the accepted spec without an explicit decision that password-only users should lose the re-auth fast path in passkeys realms.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a real behavior broadening in `UsernameForm.authenticate`: the re-auth fast-path `if (context.getUser() != null) { context.success(); }` is now gated by `&& !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`. This means in any realm where conditional passkeys are enabled, re-authentication will no longer skip the username step even when the user is already identified, and this is independent of whether the user actually has any WebAuthn/passkey credential (the gate is realm/feature-driven, not credential-driven in this diff). That’s a legitimate scope/UX change beyond just “fix re-authentication with passkeys”, but it’s not demonstrably a correctness defect from the diff alone. Note: the cited new test `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`, so it does not “bake in” the broadened behavior for passkeys-enabled realms.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Replacing the direct `user != null` check with the overridable shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context) hook, which the conditional-UI subclass hard-codes to false, silently disables the existing two-factor WebAuthn page's authenticator list in the conditional flow without that being part of the stated fix. The WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator subclass (WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:63-65) returns false unconditionally, so any deployment where the conditional-UI authenticator was rendering the authenticator picker in a 2FA step now gets the generic non-identified form instead; this is an objective change to the 2FA render path shipped under a re-auth bugfix title, and out-of-tree subclasses of WebAuthnAuthenticator that did not anticipate the new hook inherit the old behavior while conditional-UI users silently lose theirs.

adjudication.rationale: The diff objectively changes `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` from `if (user != null)` to an overridable `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` hook (defaulting to `context.getUser() != null`). `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` now overrides that hook to `return false;`, so when `fillContextForm()` is invoked on the conditional-UI authenticator it will no longer execute the branch that builds and exposes the `WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean` list for an already-identified user. That is a real behavior/scope change (potentially impacting any flow using the conditional-UI authenticator after user identification), but the diff also includes an explicit comment indicating intent (“Do not show authenticators during login with conditional passkeys”), so it’s not a clearly verifiable ‘bug’ from the diff alone—more a potentially breaking/architectural change that should be called out/validated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() is hard-overridden to false, so WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm never populates the user's authenticator list on any conditional-UI page, including the error path createErrorResponse which still calls fillContextForm. A user whose webauthn authenticator is used with an identified user (2-factor or error re-challenge) gets a webauthn form with no authenticators rendered; after a failed passkey attempt the error page offers no list/button to retry with a specific credential, leaving the re-authentication flow stuck and pushing users to password fallback even when a passkey is their only usable credential.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` gating on `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` and overrides that in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` to always return `false` with the stated intent: "Do not show authenticators during login with conditional passkeys". While this does mean the *authenticator list bean* won’t be populated in conditional-UI flows, the finding’s downstream claims (no webauthn retry button, flow stuck, forced password fallback even when passkey-only) are not verifiable from the diff: `createErrorResponse()` still enables conditional UI and calls `fillContextForm()`, and the added/updated tests assert the presence of the webauthn form (`//form[@id='webauth']`) across error/re-authentication scenarios, suggesting the UI is still usable without rendering an authenticator list.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The webauthn form setup was moved out of the user==null branch but is now gated on isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) which requires user != null, so on a fresh (non-reauth) login where no user is preset, fillContextForm is never invoked and the conditional-UI/discoverable-passkey data (previously set up for the anonymous username/password page) is no longer populated. Realms using the combined UsernamePasswordForm with passkeys enabled lose discoverable-passkey autofill on the initial login page; first-time logins must fall back to password, which both degrades the phishing-resistant path and contradicts the test expectation that the //form[@id='webauth'] element be present for anonymous users (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithExternalKey).

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm`, both the initial `authenticate()` path and the error `challenge(context, error, field)` now call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` only when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true, and `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` explicitly requires `user != null`. Previously, the error `challenge(...)` populated WebAuthn/passkeys data when `context.getUser() == null` (anonymous/initial login) via `if (context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()) { webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context); }`. This diff therefore removes form setup on fresh login pages where no user is preset, plausibly breaking discoverable/conditional-UI passkeys on the initial combined UsernamePasswordForm page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] When context.getUser() is already set during re-authentication and conditional passkeys are enabled, the skip-to-success shortcut is disabled and the plain username form is rendered, but the form still allows submitting a different username on a re-authentication session whose target user is fixed. During prompt=login re-authentication the user is presented an editable username field on a session already bound to a user; if the downstream validation of the re-auth flow does not enforce that the presented credential belongs to the original user, an attacker with an active session could pivot the re-auth toward a different account identity — the flow should be audited to confirm the error path (badPasswordHandler) and webauthn assertion both re-bind to the original user only.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change re-authentication behavior: `UsernameForm.authenticate` used to short-circuit to `context.success()` whenever `context.getUser() != null` (unless linked brokers), but now it only does so when `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`—so with conditional passkeys enabled, the username step will be rendered even though a user is already set. The finding’s broader “account pivot” exploitability depends on downstream behavior not shown in the diff (e.g., whether submitting a different username can override the bound user in re-auth sessions, and whether subsequent authenticators enforce the original user), so it can’t be verified as a concrete security bug from this diff alone. However, it’s a specific, diff-grounded concern that this change may re-expose an editable username input in a re-auth scenario that other new code (`AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError`) suggests is intended to keep username hidden/locked during re-auth error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The first 'webauthn button absent' check in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey asserts nothing because the catch(Exception) swallows the AssertionError from assertThat(..., nullValue()). If the webauthn form is wrongly rendered on the initial login page (the exact regression the test exists to catch), assertThat throws AssertionError, which is caught by catch(Exception nsee), the fail() line is never reached, and the test still passes green — the assertion provides zero verification of 'passkeys should not be shown'.

adjudication.rationale: In `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey()`, the code wraps `MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue());` in `try { ... } catch (Exception nsee) {}`. If the WebAuthn form is present, `findElement(...)` returns a non-null `WebElement` and `assertThat(..., nullValue())` throws an `AssertionError` (which extends `Error`, not `Exception`), so it is NOT swallowed by `catch (Exception)` and the test will fail as intended. If the element is absent, `findElement(...)` throws `NoSuchElementException` (an `Exception`), which is caught and treated as expected absence. So the finding's claim that the assertion provides “zero verification” because the `AssertionError` is swallowed is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The second 'webauthn button absent' check in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey has the same try/catch swallowing the AssertionError, and additionally the enclosing catch makes the fail() call unreachable whenever findElement succeeds. The re-authentication page assertion 'passkeys login should not be available as this user does not have a passkey' is unconditionally satisfied: both outcomes (element absent -> NoSuchElementException caught; element present -> AssertionError caught) lead to a passing test, so the core claim of this new test is never actually verified.

[ADVISORY] No test in the diff asserts the actual effect of setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError — that USERNAME_HIDDEN and REGISTRATION_DISABLED are set on the form when re-authentication fails. The re-authentication tests (webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey) assert the error message and the presence of the webauthn form after a bad password, but never assert that the username input is hidden or registration is disabled; a regression that re-displays the username field on the re-auth error page (the original bug this refactor re-implements) would pass all new tests. Checked: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java, PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java, PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.java contain no assertion of a hidden username field or registration-disabled state.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new nontrivial logic in `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(...)` that conditionally sets `LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN` and `LoginFormsProvider.REGISTRATION_DISABLED` based on the auth note `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` (new static import, and constant made `public` in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator`). This is now invoked from `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler(...)` and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse(...)`. The added/modified tests (e.g., `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey`) assert the re-auth info message and that the WebAuthn form is present after an invalid password, but do not assert that the username field is hidden or registration is disabled on the error page. So the finding about missing test coverage for the specific new behavior is supported by the diff; it's a test-gap concern rather than a verifiable functional defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication (and its copy in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest) never verifies the login form was actually shown before the re-auth login — the test opens prompt=login and immediately asserts appPage.assertCurrent(), so it cannot distinguish conditional-UI auto-login from the browser reusing the existing SSO session. If the prompt=login re-auth request were silently satisfied by the existing session without any passkey ceremony (defeating the point of re-authentication), the appPage.assertCurrent() and the LOGIN event assertion would still pass because the event details match the earlier auto-login pattern; a regression where UsernameForm skips and SSO short-circuits re-auth would go undetected. The author's counter-argument is that events.expectLogin().assertEvent() would fail if no new LOGIN event is produced — but a reuse of the prior session can still emit a LOGIN event with the same details, so the finding survives.

adjudication.rationale: In both newly added tests `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication()` (in `PasskeysUsernameFormTest` and `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest`), the re-auth step does `oauth.loginForm().prompt(OIDCLoginProtocol.PROMPT_VALUE_LOGIN).open(); WaitUtils.waitForPageToLoad();` and then immediately `appPage.assertCurrent()` followed by `events.expectLogin()...assertEvent()`, without asserting that any re-auth UI (login/passkey ceremony page) was actually shown. From the diff, there is no check like `loginPage.assertCurrent()` or presence of a WebAuthn form/button during the prompt=login request, so the test does not distinguish “real re-authentication happened” vs “user was redirected straight back to the app”. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage weakness rather than a product defect proven by the diff.
